correctness.rationale: Normalize any weight-three BCH polynomial by shift/scalar to 1+a x^i+b x^j. Its two zero checks eliminate the second locator and force a(a+b)X^2+2aX+(b+1)=0. Since m odd, an element of degree at most two in F_(p^m) lies in F_p, even if quadratic degenerates; the same holds for the second locator. Thus h divides both i,j; the associated P(x^h) must vanish at beta and beta^2 and be divisible by g=(x^h-beta)(x^h-beta^2). Conversely g expands to three nonzero coefficients because beta has order p-1>=4; its checks at alpha,alpha^2 vanish, so all cyclic shifts lie among weight-three codewords and generate <g>. The code has dimension n-2m from distinct size-m cyclotomic classes of 1 and 2, giving p^[2(h-m)] cosets. Boundary p>=5, odd m>=3 are essential; independent symbolic field/divisibility proof, not finite experiment alone. Inspected F_125 verifier is a limited n=124 anchor.

value.rationale: The minimum-weight-generated subcode is the natural Cayley-graph connectivity subgroup in the motivating strict function-correcting-code application. Exact symbolic description and component count for every p>=5 and odd m>=3 replace prior necessary containment/bounds with a complete structural determination.

final_claim: For every prime p>=5, every odd m>=3, primitive C_{1,2} BCH code of length n=p^m-1, h=n/(p-1), beta=alpha^h, the span of its weight-three words is precisely <(x^h-beta)(x^h-beta^2)> of dimension n-2h, and its weight-three Cayley graph has exactly p^[2(h-m)] connected components.
limitations: Does not cover p=3, even extension degree, or base field F_(p^e) for e>1.
The finite p=5,m=3 field check does not prove the universal result.
